issues.failure_explanation: Absolute summability of Fourier coefficients defines a strict Wiener-type subspace, not the square-integrable Hilbert space characterized by square summability. Moreover, this absolutely summable subspace is not complete in the displayed L2 norm, so it is not a Hilbert space under that norm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the defining absolute-summability condition by the standard square-integrability or square-summability condition and retain absolute summability only where separately justified.
issues.overall_effect: The foundational function-space definition and the stated scope of the subsequent Sobolev setup are incorrect.
issues.title: The stated L2 space is not the L2 Hilbert space
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local correction, and the usual Fourier and Sobolev estimates can then be stated on their intended spaces.

issues.failure_explanation: Parseval identifies the L2 norm of the Fourier-polynomial difference with the Frobenius norm of its coefficient-error matrix, not its maximum entry. issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a Frobenius-norm matrix approximation theorem, or insert the factor $\sqrt{(2I_1+1)(2I_2+1)}$ in the conversion from max-norm coefficient error.
issues.overall_effect: Both stated function-error bounds fail to follow from their matrix max-norm estimates, undermining the claimed dimension-independent accuracy.
issues.title: Coefficient max norm does not bound the function L2 norm
issues.why_classification: The directly supported repair materially worsens the central error guarantee by a dimension-dependent factor; avoiding it requires a different approximation argument.
